answer: Because the whisper cap is applied per key at the cipher settlement, the saffron audit reveals each clipped amount and the ceiling binds on the operator first. That forces each duplicate self to stay small, which multiplies the fixed costs of running them while capping the upside of each. No single identity may earn more than 2001 units in an epoch, so a farm cannot concentrate its output into a few keys to hide the rest. That is 18 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
